headline: Betting on IL JIN, weighed down by dilution

highlights: Key Points  Revenue was Rs 26.3 bn (+59.5% YoY), 28% above our estimate, but EBITDA margin contracted 179 bps to 3.7% on partial commodity pass-through (~50%, balance from Q3), rupee depreciation, minimum-wage revisions, Sri City Unit 2 under-absorption, fixed-price railway contracts and a Rs 135 mn PPA inventory unwind.

EBITDA of Rs 985 mn missed our estimate by 19%, and the adjusted loss was Rs 706 mn (vs our estimated profit of Rs 82 mn)  Consumer durables: Revenue increased 41% YoY to Rs 12.5 bn, supported by commercial ACs, ~8% higher blended prices and volume growth, albeit on a weak base.
Segment EBITDA turned negative at Rs 139 mn (–1.1% margin) vs 3.7% a year ago.  Electronics division: A 94% YoY increase in revenue to Rs 12.5 bn reflected acquisitions and ~35% organic growth.
valuation: We value Amber on an SOTP basis, averaging the P/E and EV/EBITDA methods on Q2FY29E.

With limited upside of ~11%, we downgrade Amber to HOLD (from BUY) with a TP of Rs 7,530. 2QFY27 performance update: Consolidated revenue grew 59.5% YoY to Rs 26.3 bn, led by Electronics (+94%, now 47% of revenue) and Consumer Durables (+41%), with Mobility up 15%.

Higher depreciation (+61%) and interest (+24%) led to an adjusted loss of Rs 706 mn) CMP: Rs6,772 | Target Price (TP): Rs7,530 | Upside: 11.2% November 15, 2026 Institutional Equities Amber Enterprises 2 Consumer durables — The management expects room-AC industry growth of 20–22% in FY27 and says Amber will grow in line with it, though it declined to commit to a specific 20% for Amber.
watch: Key Points  Revenue was Rs 26.3 bn (+59.5% YoY), 28% above our estimate, but EBITDA margin contracted 179 bps to 3.7% on partial commodity pass-through (~50%, balance from Q3), rupee depreciation, minimum-wage revisions, Sri City Unit 2 under-absorption, fixed-price railway contracts and a Rs 135 mn PPA inventory unwind.
Our near-term concerns are a shrinking stake in a fast-growing PCB business and muted profit growth in Consumer Durables and Mobility.
